topic: What power allocation trade-offs arise from differing scan losses between quasi-TEM and quasi-TE1 modes for multi-beam satellite systems?
consensus_response: The differing scan losses between quasi-TEM and quasi-TE1 modes significantly impact the power allocation trade-offs in multi-beam satellite systems. Quasi-TEM modes offer more efficient power allocation, reducing scan losses and increasing beam efficiency. Conversely, quasi-TE1 modes require more power due to higher scan losses, leading to reduced beam efficiency and increased power consumption. To optimize system efficiency, satellite operators can employ flexible power allocation techniques, such as spatial power combining in a multiple carrier/HPA configuration. However, this flexibility comes at the expense of reduced power advantage of TDM over OFDM due to the need for sufficient back off. In high-user-demand scenarios, power allocation trade-offs become more critical, requiring judicious power allocation to balance the needs of both original and new satellite users while accounting for varying interference pricing and path loss conditions.
